rest.note: the defaults; restMeasured is what the feed says

restMeasured.computed: from baseline.json and demand.json, 1986 timed lines, 2,899,346 commuters in the fit, 2026-09-08

sources.noCar: 83.7 per cent of households have no private car available: 16.3 per cent have one or more (Transport Department, Travel Characteristics Survey 2022, table 4.1; notes/cities/hongkong.md)
sources.twoWheelShare: initial estimate from 5.1 per cent of households having a bicycle available; the survey warns that cycling is under-reported and publishes no all-trip share (Transport Department, Travel Characteristics Survey 2022; notes/cities/hongkong.md)
sources.car: fuel about HK$2,200 and parking HK$2,700 per month for a private car in 2022 (Transport Department, Travel Characteristics Survey 2022, table 4.3); EUR0.24/km, EUR3 a trip and five minutes to park are explicit modelling estimates until a trip-level cost source is found
sources.votSPerEur: the Transport Department's weighted behavioural value of time is HK$0.90 a minute in 2022; at HK$8.5 to EUR1 this is EUR6.35 an hour, or 567 seconds a euro, rounded to 570
sources.commute: 31 minutes is the published mean for all private-vehicle and taxi trips, not work trips (Transport Department, Travel Characteristics Survey 2022, table E.2); it is the closest official mode-specific proxy and is labelled as such
sources.capexCostFactor: Shatin to Central Link cost HK$79.8B for 17 km, HK$4.69B/km, or about EUR552M/km at HK$8.5/EUR; Berlin's U5 benchmark is EUR239M/km, giving 2.3 (Hong Kong Legislative Council; notes/cities/hongkong.md)
sources.capexProgrammeM: Railway Development Strategy 2014 estimated seven projects at HK$110B in 2013 prices, about EUR12.9B at HK$8.5/EUR; this is a programme benchmark, not a current appropriation
sources.capexAwardFactor: first balance setting: permanent awards use a separate 2.3 factor, matching the construction-cost factor rather than the 86-fold opening-programme scale; approved 2026-09-08, not a calibrated optimum (notes/hongkong-release-audit-2026-09-08.md)

timetables.text: Hong Kong Transport Department public GTFS, with MTR routes and service ranges from official MTR tables

signs.note: MTR uses line abbreviations. Hong Kong Tramways and buses use route numbers
